title: Radius from a half-chord and the distance to the centre
source: Theory IGCSE-19.3 Quick check 1; 3-4-5 family, chord 8k, distance 3k, radius 5k
stem: A chord of a circle is \({C|int}\) cm long and is \({D|int}\) cm from the centre. Find the radius of the circle, in centimetres.

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: Each half-chord is \({k|int}\times 4\) cm, and \(r^2=({D|int})^2+({k|int}\times 4)^2\), so \(r={A|int}\).
steps.note: Pythagoras with the half-chord and the distance from the centre.

contexts.note: Includes the original chord 8 cm, distance 3 cm

title: Length of a chord from the radius and the distance to the centre
source: Theory IGCSE-19.3 Quick check 2; 5-12-13 family, radius 13k, distance 5k, chord 24k
stem: A chord of a circle of radius \({R|int}\) cm is \({D|int}\) cm from the centre. Find the length of the chord, in centimetres.

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: Half the chord is \(\sqrt{({R|int})^2-({D|int})^2}={k|int}\times 12\), so the chord is \({A|int}\) cm long.

contexts.note: Includes the original radius 13 cm, distance 5 cm

title: Distance between two equal chords on opposite sides of the centre
source: Theory IGCSE-19.3 Quick check 3; two equal chords on opposite sides, each n cm from the centre, are 2n cm apart
stem: A chord of a circle is \({n|int}\) cm from the centre. A second chord of the same length lies on the opposite side of the centre. Find the distance, in centimetres, between the two chords.

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: Equal chords are equidistant from the centre, so the two chords are each \({n|int}\) cm from the centre and on opposite sides. The distance between them is \({A|int}\) cm.
steps.note: Equal chords are equidistant from the centre.

contexts.note: Includes the original 8 cm from the centre, distance 16 cm
